analyst_view.overall: Early view: a lunchtime game between fifth and fourth, three days after both play midweek (Chelsea against Palace, Liverpool against Sunderland). Chelsea were beaten at Sunderland and have conceded the most non-penalty set-piece goals in the league, while Liverpool under Iraola have the best away record with 13 points. Liverpool's press and set-piece strength against Chelsea's soft spots is the main angle.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean slightly lower: Liverpool's games have averaged well under three goals and they concede about one a game, and both teams come in tired three days after a midweek match. Chelsea's set-piece weakness is the main route to more goals.

corners.text: The site has 10.4 corners. I agree: both sides will have spells of pressure, and Liverpool will look to win corners against a Chelsea side that has conceded eight non-penalty set-piece goals. Nothing points far from the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards. I agree: a big game with Liverpool's intense press and Chelsea losing duels at Sunderland suggests fouls, and Alexis Mac Allister was booked at home to Arsenal. Around five is fair.

shots.text: The site has 28.4 shots. I lean slightly lower: the early kick-off after a midweek game and two sides who can be cautious in big matches (Liverpool's away wins have been controlled) point to a slightly slower game. Mid-20s looks likely.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. I lean lower: Liverpool managed none on target at home to Arsenal and Chelsea produced little at Sunderland, with Joao Pedro still injured. Eight on target seems more realistic.
